title: ISRO's First 2026 Launch, PSLV-C62/EOS-N1, Fails to Reach Orbit
shortDescription: PSLV-C62 lifted off on 12 January 2026 carrying the EOS-N1 (Anvesha) satellite and 14 co-passengers, but a third-stage deviation meant the payloads were lost — ISRO's second consecutive PSLV setback.
genZNote: Liftoff ≠ mission success. Early headlines said 'successful launch' — the actual outcome, confirmed later, was FAILURE. Read status labels, not just the first headline.

sections.heading: What Happened
sections.body: On 12 January 2026, ISRO launched the PSLV-C62 mission — the 64th flight of the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle — from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, carrying the DRDO-built EOS-N1 (also called Anvesha) earth observation satellite plus 14 co-passenger payloads. The rocket lifted off successfully, but a deviation in the third stage meant the satellites failed to reach their intended sun-synchronous orbit — the mission is recorded as a FAILURE, ISRO's second consecutive PSLV setback.

sections.heading: Key Facts
bullets: Mission: PSLV-C62, 64th flight of the PSLV ('Workhorse of ISRO').
Primary payload: EOS-N1 (Anvesha), a DRDO-built earth observation satellite.
Launch: 10:17 AM IST, 12 January 2026, First Launch Pad, Satish Dhawan Space Centre.
Co-passengers: 14 domestic and international satellites, including contributions from Indian private firm Dhruva Space and a European re-entry demonstrator capsule (KID).
OUTCOME: Failure — a deviation in the rocket's third stage prevented the satellites from reaching orbit.
This followed an earlier PSLV setback (PSLV-C61, EOS-09) in 2025 — making it two consecutive PSLV failures.

sections.heading: Why It Matters
sections.body: This is a good reminder that same-day news coverage of a launch ('successful liftoff') can differ from the confirmed final mission outcome once post-flight data is reviewed — exam questions on ISRO missions should be answered from the confirmed OUTCOME, not the initial headline.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: PSLV-C62, ISRO's first launch of 2026 (12 January), lifted off successfully but failed to place the EOS-N1 satellite into orbit due to a third-stage deviation.
keyFacts: Primary payload: EOS-N1 (Anvesha), built by DRDO.
commonConfusion: "Successful liftoff" (the rocket left the pad correctly) is not the same as "successful mission" (the payload reached its intended orbit) — this mission had the first without the second.

highYieldFacts: EOS-N1 = DRDO-built; failed to reach orbit due to a PSLV third-stage deviation on 12 Jan 2026.
commonTraps: Citing PSLV-C62 as a 'successful' 2026 ISRO mission based only on early liftoff reports.
mustRemember: PSLV-C62/EOS-N1, 12 Jan 2026 — LAUNCHED but FAILED to reach orbit.
